title: OCC Invite #broadway #musicaltheatre #sunsetboulevard #westend #nicol...
transcript: I kinda hated watching the Sunset Boulevard revival but it may or may not be for the reasons you think some of you won't believe me but I actually went into this production really optimistic and eager to love it eager to see a director that I admire present an aggressively new take on this material and like I know a lot of people have been comparing this to Ballroom Cats but like yes I'm in that camp too the fact that I loved Ballroom Cats as much as I did made me even more optimistic that I would love this production of Sunset but to my profound disappointment it turns out that even I was underestimating just how excruciating I find this material cause guess what? I actually loved what Jamie Lloyd did with it not only the striking stage pictures not only the smart use of technical elements and movement also just loved the whole meta self aware concept and how Nicole Scherzinger's performance was so integral to that and I can even say that you know I had my doubts beforehand but I am now Team “Walk” but despite all of that I just couldn't get over how much I hate this musical and I need you to believe me that I tried I tried so hard but I hated this show when I saw it on Broadway in 2017 and I hate it just as much now it is like nails on a chalkboard to me it is a sensitive to my sensibilities and there's a lot of different reasons I could point to one of which is that I can't for the life of me bring myself to care about anything that happens with Joe or Betty and that takes up a surprising amount of the runtime But really more than anything else it's the score and don't get me wrong I love “as if we never said goodbye” and “with one look” as much as the next guy but as I have always said the great con of the Andrew Lloyd Webber empire is that he writes one or two really good songs per show and then half-🫏es the rest of it and there is no greater example of that than Sunset Boulevard where the words “lazy” and “repetitive” do not even begin to scratch the surface and of course I don't mind when a composer reuses a motif or melody throughout a show for storytelling purposes but when it's the same four cloying bars played back to back for like five minutes like what do you want from me? if I have to listen to 🎵 🎵 🎵🎵 🎶🎵🎵 or like what's the other one with Betty where they're like 🎶🎵🎵 if I have to listen to either of those two melodies one more time for the rest of my god forsaken life I swear to god I'll quit and go Amish so like I said I loved Jamie Lloyd's direction but here's the thing at least half of what it takes to put on a good revival is choice of material and for that reason I can't comfortably call this a good revival now what I would have really loved is for the Jamie Lloyd Company to commission a new adaptation of the original movie and do everything else the exact same then I would have loved it and hell if they could get permission to throw “as if we never said goodbye” in there just for good measure then I'm on board with that too but otherwise I'm happy to let this material rot in obscurity like Norma Desmond herself
reasoning: The reviewer explicitly states he 'hated' watching the show and deeply dislikes the source material/score, despite praising Jamie Lloyd's direction and Nicole Scherzinger's performance. He cannot call it a 'good revival' because he fundamentally dislikes the material, and his overall experience was clearly negative.
